name: Hlane Royal National Park
blurb: Bushveld, white rhino and the densest nesting vultures in Africa.

tip.title: Thin the impala
tip.text: Impala are prey for lions, cheetah and hyenas, and their carcasses feed vultures. Lower impala and watch the predators and scavengers respond.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: A thorny hardwood tree of the bushveld. Wikipedia lists knobthorn among the ancient hardwoods of Hlane, and GloBI records giraffe browsing it.
A thorny tree whose leaves and fruit are recorded in the diet of impala, warthog, waterbuck and baboons.

nodes.name: Savanna grasses
nodes.desc: The grassy layer between the trees, fed by the summer rains. It is the main food for the grazers, such as rhino, zebra and wildebeest.
Wikipedia lists impala among the park herbivores. It eats both browse and grass, and gathers at waterholes in the dry winter.
A large antelope recorded here eating sicklebush and buffalo thorn. It stays close to water and grass.

nodes.name: Southern giraffe
nodes.desc: Wikipedia lists giraffe in the park. It browses the crowns of tall trees such as knobthorn.
The largest browser in the park. GloBI records it eating sicklebush, giant donkeyberry and wild vines.
Eats grass and roots, and is recorded eating sicklebush and buffalo thorn. It is common prey for lions.
A grazer that, with zebra and impala, gathers at waterholes in the dry winter months.
A grazer of the savanna grass layer. It is listed among the park herbivores and is a regular lion prey.
Wikipedia notes cheetah were reintroduced to Hlane after a long absence. It hunts medium antelope such as impala.
Both a hunter and a scavenger. GloBI records it feeding on many of the park herbivores.
Wikipedia says Hlane has the highest density of nesting white-backed vultures in Africa. It eats the soft tissue of large herbivore carcasses.
The park top predator. GloBI records it eating impala, wildebeest, zebra, warthog and giraffe, among others.
Rain falls mostly from December to March, and the Lowveld gets roughly 200 to 550 mm a year. This sets how much the trees and grass grow.
The Lowveld is hot in summer, with temperatures reaching around 40 C. Sun powers growth of all the plants.
Nutrients in the soil feed the trees and grasses, and are returned by decay of dead plants and animals.
Fungi, bacteria and insects break down dead plants, dung and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil.

story: Hlane Royal National Park covers 300 km² of Eswatini as a flat lowland area of Swazi bushveld. It is Eswatini's largest protected area and park, featuring ancient hardwood trees, grasslands, and shallow pans where lion, elephant, South African giraffe, and white rhinoceros live.
matters: The park provides a vital sanctuary and the highest density of nesting white-backed vultures in Africa. It preserves a diverse ecosystem supporting rich birdlife and large mammals within the region.
